page: Microsoft Azure D96d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine hypervised by Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C x86_64 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores via hyper-threading. The architecture integrates 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and support for AVX-512 and VAES vector extensions. The instance is provisioned with 384 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware provisioning also bundles 3,865 GB of high-speed local SSD storage without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate pronounced multi-threaded throughput alongside moderate single-threaded capability. The instance recorded 93,235.13 on stress-ng multi-core and 17,390.0 on Geekbench multi-core tests, placing it in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is substantial, achieving 315.9 GB/sec read and 134.24 GB/sec write on uncached blocks. Cryptographic throughput is an operational highlight, with PassMark encryption scoring 87,610.78 in the top 10 percent due to hardware AES and SHA support. In contrast, single-thread stress-ng scored 1,896.19 and Geekbench single-core scored 1,646.0, reflecting standard clock performance rather than specialized high-frequency execution. CPU-based machine learning inference performs solidly on small models but drops to 2.69 tokens per second on large 70B parameter models due to the absence of dedicated tensor hardware.

Cost efficiency for the D96d_v5 is defined by its balanced density, pairing massive parallel compute capacity with expansive integrated NVMe-class storage. The inclusion of 3,865 GB local SSD reduces the need for costly attached volume tiers when handling ephemeral storage tasks. The architecture is well matched for scalable multi-threaded services, high-throughput static web hosting, parallel software compilation, and in-memory caches, as proven by 86.66 million Redis SET operations per second and 30,560.3 PassMark database marks.
description: Microsoft Azure D96d_v5 is a high-density, general-purpose cloud instance configured with 96 vCPUs across 48 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores at 2.8 GHz, 384 GB of memory, and 3,865 GB of local SSD storage. Designed without discrete GPUs, it adheres to a standard 1:4 core-to-memory distribution. Benchmark profiles highlight top-tier cryptographic operations alongside strong multi-core processing, achieving 93,235.13 on multi-core stress-ng tests and high uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 315 GB/sec. Single-threaded metrics remain within the median range across comparable hardware. Its substantial embedded SSD pool and rapid memory read and write pipelines reduce I/O bottlenecks without requiring separate storage attachments. The instance profile is optimal for enterprise transactional databases, Redis caching layers, concurrent Clang builds, and data ingestion pipelines requiring extensive local temporary scratch space.
